question: Using Figure 2A-1 and Section 2A.11, describe the requirements for a retroreflective strip used on a sign support to enhance conspicuity.
model_answer: Direct Answer: Using a retroreflective strip on a sign support is a permitted conspicuity-enhancement method chosen by engineering judgment, but once used it must meet mandatory dimensions and placement. The strip must be at least 2 inches wide, run the full length of the support from the sign to within 2 feet above the near edge of the roadway, match the sign's background color (red for YIELD and DO NOT ENTER signs), and carry no legend. A related mandatory application exists for Crossbuck supports at passive grade crossings, where a white retroreflective strip is required on the back of each support. Standards (mandatory): - "If a strip of retroreflective material is used on the sign support, it shall be at least 2 inches in width, it shall be placed for the full length of the support from the sign to within 2 feet above the near edge of the roadway, and its color shall match the background color of the sign, except that the color of the strip for the YIELD and DO NOT ENTER signs shall be red. The retroreflective strip shall not display any legend or other information." - For passive grade crossings: "A vertical strip of retroreflective white material, not less than 2 inches in width, shall be used on each Crossbuck support at passive grade crossings for the full length of the back of the support from the Crossbuck sign or Number of Tracks plaque to within 2 feet above the near edge of the roadway... A white retroreflective strip wrapped around a round support... shall satisfy this requirement as long as the round support has an outside diameter of at least 2 inches." Options (permitted): - Based on engineering judgment, where improvement of the conspicuity of a standard regulatory, warning, or guide sign is desired, adding a strip of retroreflective material to the sign support (see Figure 2A-1) may be used as one of the listed conspicuity-enhancement methods. Visual evidence: - [Image 1] Figure 2A-1, panel E ("Vertical retroreflective strip on sign support"), depicts a fluorescent yellow-green strip matching the pedestrian sign's background color running down the support and terminating with a "2 ft MAX." dimension above the near edge of the roadway. - [Image 2] The full-page view of Figure 2A-1 (p.48) confirms the strip is one of seven illustrated conspicuity-enhancement examples (A–G) referenced in Section 2A.11. - [Image 3] The page containing Section 2A.21 notes that "Information regarding the use of retroreflective material on the sign support is contained in Section 2A.11." - [Image 4] The page containing Section 2A.11 shows the Standard text (Paragraph 5) with the 2-inch width, full-length placement, 2-foot termination, color-matching, and no-legend requirements. - [Image 5] Figure 8B-2 illustrates the Crossbuck Assembly application, showing a "2-inch white retroreflective strip on back of support," an "Optional 2-inch red or white retroreflective strip on front of support," and the "2 ft MAX." termination above the edge of roadway. Citations: - Section 2A.11 Standard §5 (p.49) - Section 2A.11 Option §1 (p.49) - Section 2A.21 Support §8 (p.62) - Section 8B.04 Standard §17 (p.1000) - Figure 2A-1 (p.48) - Page 89 - Page 103 - Page 90 - Page 1038
gold_answer: The strip must be at least 2 inches wide, extend from the sign down the full support to within 2 feet above the near edge of the roadway, match the sign background color except that YIELD and DO NOT ENTER strips are red, and contain no legend or other information.
